title: Who controls the agent that moves your money
dek: Wells Fargo, a sandbox and a checkout flow each put limits around AI agents.

body.head: Agent access gets written into contracts
body.text: Wells Fargo is updating its Online Access Agreement, effective November 24, 2026, and the update covers third-party AI tools. Requests submitted through such a tool may be treated as if they came directly from the user, and the bank also reserves the right to restrict or block access from certain tools.
support: We wanted to let you know we're updating our Online Access Agreement (“Agreement”), effective November 24, 2026 , which covers your use of Wells Fargo's online and mobile services.

The information shared with the tool will be subject to the provider's privacy practices and terms, requests submitted through the tool may be treated as if they came directly from you, and we included your responsibilities for managing the tool's access to your accounts.
We also reserve the right to restrict or block access from certain third-party AI tools.

body.head: A sandbox to test agent controls
body.text: The Future of Finance Institute will set up an Agentic Money Sandbox, a controlled environment where financial institutions can test how AI agents transact using digital money within defined authority, limits and safeguards. DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB are the launch partners, and the initial use cases are agent-initiated payments and treasury management.
support: FFI will establish an Agentic Money Sandbox, which provides a controlled environment for financial institutions to develop and test how AI agents can transact using digital money within defined authority, limits and safeguards.
Initial use cases will include agent-initiated payments and treasury management across participating financial institutions.
MAS and FFI also unveiled FFI’s financial institutions launch partners — DBS, OCBC, Standard Chartered and UOB — at SFF 2026.

body.head: Checkout keeps a human confirmation
body.text: Klarna has become the first payment option beyond cards available in Adyen's agentic commerce suite, the two companies said in a press release, and shoppers will review and confirm the purchase before it is completed, the release said.
support: Klarna has become the first payment option beyond cards available in Adyen ’s agentic commerce suite, Adyen Agentic , the two companies said in a Friday (Nov. 20) press release .

Shoppers will be shown the same Klarna options the merchant already offers, such as paying in full, in interest-free installments or with financing, and will then review and confirm the purchase before it is completed, the release said.

body.head: A question for your own team
body.text: Laid side by side, the three stories each describe a limit on what an agent may do: a contract term, a sandbox with defined authority, and a confirmation step at checkout. For those of us who work in banks and payment firms, a useful question this week is which of those three limits our own products already have, and who owns each one.
